Where I got to
I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt and verified it: 348 of 349 files byte-identical to their recorded SHA-256. The exception is export.sh, which contains the dump's own # FILE: banner as literal text and cannot be round-tripped by any parser using that banner as a delimiter — excluded from the work set, not guessed at, and not delivered.

The tree is further along than I had it. Specification is at v1.28, not v1.25; Slice 43 closed MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync with its picker on ManageMenuItem, which was the last verb in the whole enhancement without a surface. Last observed test count 1151; Slice 43 predicts 1157. docs/_append/ is gone from the tree, ManageMenuSection.razor and ManageMenuItem.razor both exist, and every one of the six deferred IMenuWorkflow verbs is discharged.

So the largest remaining piece of Stage 3 is the one the last slice named as unblocked: /administration/menu becoming sections-first rather than a flat item list with a Section column.

What I had started building (Slice 44)
app.css — a new .menu-group* vocabulary, declared once, no new breakpoint, no colour literal, no var() fallback, --touch-target on the summary. Done. Plus the one wide-layout rule inside the existing min-width: 48rem query. Done.
AdministrationMenu.razor — rewritten as a list of headings, each a <details> rendered open, holding its own items as a .record-list. This is where the limit hit: I had just removed the old file and had not yet written the replacement. The tree I hold is currently missing that file — nothing is delivered from this session, so your repository is untouched, but I want to be explicit that the work-in-progress is incomplete rather than pretend otherwise.
The ruling I need your veto on before I finish
The plan says the sections-first index arrives "with the section's own order controls." I am going to cut that and record the cut, for a concrete reason rather than for room:

ReorderMenuSectionAsync sets an absolute display_order, and positions are deliberately non-unique with a name tiebreak. So "move this heading up" is not expressible as one absolute write — two headings sharing a position have an order nobody assigned, and no single number distinguishes them. An honest Up/Down needs a resequencing verb writing several rows and therefore several reordered events in one transaction: a new write with new event semantics, not a surface change. The index will instead make the ordering visible (headings in stored order, position on each group) and keep the write on the editor.

Two smaller consequences I also intend:

HandheldReach.cs's reach selector must gain .menu-group-summary and .menu-group-actions a. Without it, replacing measured .record-actions rows with unmeasured groups would silently shrink scenario 16's coverage on a surface it already walks — and scenario 16's own account of itself ("every row's way in lies inside the viewport") would become false of this page.
Empty headings become visible on this surface for the first time. The old index was built from items, so a heading with nothing under it was invisible — its own code comment says so. Worth a paragraph, and worth an end-to-end step: scenario 17 gains a third heading with nothing in it, and the assertion is the disagreement between the two surfaces — three groups on the administrator's index, two groupings on the guest's menu, and the difference is exactly the empty one.
Say "continue" and I'll write the remaining files and deliver the structured .tar.gz extractable at the repo root, with full files throughout (AdministrationMenu.razor, app.css, HandheldReach.cs, HandheldLayoutContractTests.cs, AdministrationJourneys.cs, EndToEndScenarios.cs, specification to v1.29, DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, BUILD_PROGRESS.md whole, _CHANGES.md), a "Files to DELETE" section, and git add reminders. If you'd rather the order controls ship instead of the cut, say so now — it changes what the slice is.
